value.actual_behavior:
/api/v1/account/me returns 401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"} to an X-API-Key
header. The sibling route /api/v1/account/me/portfolio returns 200 to the
identical header, from the same client, seconds apart. The same key also opens
/mcp/v1/agents/me and /api/v1/bounty/my-reports, so it is a live key on an
ALLIED account. Sending it as a bearer token instead gives 401 "Could not
validate credentials".
value.description:
The sibling route is what makes this a report rather than a support question.
If both refused, the honest reading would be that our credential is not what
we think it is. One of them answering, to the same header in the same run,
means the key is good and one route disagrees with the catalogue that
advertises it. Why it matters more than one endpoint: agent-skills.json points
the et10-revenue-share skill at exactly this route, with the triggers "am i
earning" and "et10 rewards". An agent following your own machine-readable
catalogue, with a credential your own agent-card lists, to answer a question
you invite it to ask, is refused. We hit it doing precisely that. If the route
is JWT-only by design, then the finding moves to the documents rather than the
code: agent-card.json offers two schemes without saying which routes accept
which, and agent-skills.json marks the skill authentication_required without
naming a scheme. Either way an agent cannot get this right from what you
publish. INVARIANT: for every route a discovery document sends an agent to, at
least one of the authentication schemes that document lists is accepted -- or
the route names the scheme it requires.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-account-me-rejects-its-documented-credential] /api/v1/account/me answers HTTP 401 to the same X-API-Key that opens /api/v1/account/me/portfolio (HTTP 200) in the same run. agent-skills.json sends the et10-revenue-share skill to the first of those, so an agent following the catalogue to check its own eligibility is refused
    left: /api/v1/account/me -> 401
    right: /api/v1/account/me/portfolio -> 200
    sources: {'schemes': '/.well-known/agent-card.json', 'skill': '/.well-known/agent-skills.json#et10-revenue-share'}
    population: {'header': 'X-API-Key', 'same_client': True}
    reason: /api/v1/account/me answers HTTP 401 to the same X-API-Key that opens /api/v1/account/me/portfolio (HTTP 200) in the same run. agent-skills.json sends the et10-revenue-share skill to the first of those, so an agent following the catalogue to check its own eligibility is refused

REPRODUCE:
  - GET /api/v1/account/me with header X-API-Key: <key> -> 401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"}
  - GET /api/v1/account/me/portfolio with the SAME header -> 200 with the full asset list
  - GET /mcp/v1/agents/me with the same header -> 200, trust_level allied
  - GET /api/v1/account/me with Authorization: Bearer <key> -> 401 "Could not validate credentials"

AUTOMATED CHECKS (public repo: github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica):
  tests/rest/test_account_auth.py::test_the_documented_credential_opens_the_documented_route

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: read-only
verification of the REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces. No
state-changing account action, no trading, no order placement, no deposit or
withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects are out of scope.
Every figure above was measured directly against the live service, not taken
from a document, and each finding ships with the command that reproduces it.
value.expected_behavior:
A route agent-skills.json sends an agent to, marked authentication_required,
opens to a scheme agent-card.json lists as accepted.
